career.title: The Baker
career.workplace: The Stone Oven Bakery, Baker Street
career.pitch: Five quests, five ranks, one family. You knock on a side door at four in the morning and end up deciding what a hundred-and-twenty-year-old bakery becomes. Every quest asks the same question from a new side: what do you keep, and what do you let change?

lore.title: The year the wall came down
text: Old Town had a wall once. It kept nothing out but the view. A hundred and twenty years ago the town voted, by a margin people still argue about, to take it down and use the stone for something better.

The line of it is still there if you know where to look: West Wall, North Wall, East Wall and South Wall streets run where it stood. Every street that used to end at the wall was given a tree to walk towards instead, which is why so many streets carry a tree's name. The stone went into garden walls, the fountain's basin, and one bakery oven.
lore.used: Background for everything. Explains the street names already on the map and the taken-down wall in the city data.

lore.title: The Town Oven and the brass tokens
text: Before every kitchen had its own fire, Old Town had one: the Town Oven, by the fountain in Market Square. You made your dough at home, pressed your household's brass token into the top, and carried it to the square. The baker's peel took forty loaves at a time. The token came back baked into the crust, so nobody went home with the wrong bread.

The Town Oven closed fifty-eight years ago, the winter gas came to the last streets. The tokens went into a drawer at the museum. Each one has a number, and the museum knows which family held which, with eleven exceptions that Jai considers a personal failing. Number forty-one is lent out for a year to whoever wins the Town Fair.
lore.used: The fair prize in Market Day; the Long Table ending brings the Town Oven back. The brass-token quest markers already in the slice can be read as the same tokens.

lore.title: The Mother
text: A sourdough culture is flour and water that has been kept alive: fed every day, used every day, never finished. The Stone Oven's is called the Mother. Noor's great-grandmother Ilse started her the week the wall came down, in a stoneware crock, and she has been fed at midnight and at five ever since, through two wars' worth of shortages and one flood.

Every loaf the bakery has ever sold was raised by her. She will not take roller-milled flour and never has. She is fed with wrist-warm water, never from the kettle: cold only slows a culture down, but heat kills it outright. There are two living jars of her in the world. Only one of them is known about.
lore.used: The centre of the career. Her fate in Feeding the Mother changes every later quest.

lore.title: Old Wall Red
text: When the east wall came down, the rubble that couldn't be carted was ploughed in where it lay. The soil along that line is full of mortar and drains like nowhere else in the valley. Old Wall Red is an old wheat, the kind the Town Oven's bread was made from, and it had all but died out. Forty years ago Len of Brook Farm found one forgotten sack of it and sowed it there, mostly out of stubbornness.

It yields badly, mills awkwardly, and tastes of somewhere. Roller mills can't do much with it; the silo buyers call it contamination. Put through a sharp stone, it makes the bread people from Old Town describe to strangers on trains.
lore.used: Stone Ground. Whether the Red survives decides the quality of the fair loaf.

lore.title: The last stone
text: Mill Street is named for the mills that stood along the stream when the town had six of them. Mill Works makes machine parts now. One stone mill is left, out at Mill Fields, and Oda runs it.

A millstone cuts with furrows chiselled into its face, and the furrows wear. Recutting them is called dressing the stone, done with a small pick called a mill bill, following a pattern of harps and furrows that every dresser learns from the one before. A dresser signs the stone, near the eye, with a mark of their own. The last dresser in the valley was Oda's husband Marek. His sign was an ear of wheat.
lore.used: Stone Ground: the dressing of the stones, and the choice of whose mark goes beside Marek's.

lore.title: Baker Street, four in the morning
text: Baker Street had four bakeries once and is down to one. The Stone Oven's oven was built from wall stone the year the wall came down, which is where the name comes from, and it has not gone cold on a working day since.

The shop opens at seven and is sold out by a little after nine. The side door is in the alley. Bakers use the alley. There are three keys to that door in the world, and a great deal of this career is about who holds them.
lore.used: The career's workplace and its daily rhythm.

courting.pitch: One person in the Baker's story can be courted: Mei, from the morning round. The line is three quests and then a wedding, and each step is gated the same way: her regard for you has to reach a level before the next step can even be asked.

rules.why: Lunch at 25, dinner at 45, the question at 75. A lunch that goes well reaches 45. A dinner that goes very well can reach 75 at once; one that goes only middling leaves a gap to make up with shifts at the café. From quests alone, only the kindest start reaches 25: the bread given to Mei, and your own breakfast loaf on the first round.
A lunch or a dinner that goes badly can be asked for again once her regard has recovered.

rules.what: A home and savings before she says yes
rules.why: She will say what she wants and send you away to get it: a home you own (a mortgage counts, renting does not) and 150 Bx put by. Arrive already holding both and she says yes on the spot.

A market-day event on the square. Noor bakes the loaf, because a baker does not bake their own. Who stands up with you and who is in the crowd come from how you lived the career. It ends with one choice that picks the first end-game thread.

endgame.title: Household
endgame.text: Your wife moves into the home you bought and keeps her own routine from there, out to the café before the first tram. A shared account at Linden Bank. She moves out of the flat she shares at Lantern Court.

endgame.title: Family
endgame.text: Children join the household over the years, each a new resident with a routine of their own: the school gate, the playground, the tram. More people in a house means a bigger house.

endgame.title: Fortune
endgame.text: The getting-richer thread. Buy the empty shop between the café and the oven and run all three. Then property: buy to let, the mall units, the row on Baker Street. Each step is a bank loan, a risk and a rival bidder.

endgame.title: Legacy
endgame.text: Take an apprentice and send out their first basket one loaf short. Decide, years on, whose name goes on the door after yours.

decisions.title: The dropped tray
decisions.ask: Pip drops a night's work ninety seconds before Noor comes back. Pip has known you for about a minute.

options.now: Pip is grateful, and says so. Noor says only “Hm”.
later: Noor counted the trays. Raise it at the verdict and she tells you that today was your one blind eye.
Pip pays the debt in Quest II by telling you about the jar marked MUM.

options.now: An hour of pastry owed, and “You said we. Noted.”
later: The best standing with both Noor and Pip.
Pip confides in you in Quest II, and listens to you at the fair.

options.now: “Thank you for the report.” Pip goes quiet.
later: In Quest II Pip tells you about the jar only if you ask, and with an edge.
At the fair Pip has already decided to leave for Tam's counter. Only a real apology changes that.

decisions.title: Seventeen loaves
decisions.ask: Eighteen owed, seventeen in the barrow, nobody watching. Noor shorted the basket herself to see what you would do.

options.now: The café gets its dozen. You go hungry until the verdict.
later: Hired clean. Mei tells the story for a week.
Mei's regard helps her become the Red's second buyer in Quest III.

options.pick: Go back and check the count
options.now: Eleven minutes late, and Mei lets you know it.
later: Hired clean: “A count you check is yours.”

options.pick: Short one of them, and say so
options.now: An apology at one counter or the other.
later: Hired clean, a little cooler. There was no right one to short; she wanted to hear whether you would tell her which.

options.pick: Buy a mall loaf and say nothing
options.now: Four brix. Olu turns one loaf over and decides to say nothing, to you.
later: Olu takes the loaf straight to Noor. Hired on watch at best; shrug it off and the door shuts.
The man who sold it was Tam. He recognises you in Quest II.
Olu may whisper it to Vera at the judging table in Quest IV.

decisions.title: Object OT-112
decisions.ask: The crock that could save the Mother is a museum object. Jai offers a form and a loan. There is a third way.

options.now: Noor has to face her own signature from the week her mother died.
later: Standing with both Noor and Jai. The proper way, and the one that costs Noor something.

options.pick: A loan for “demonstration of original function”
options.now: Jai wraps the crock like a christening.
later: Jai is an ally from here on. Not offered if you kept his rare book.

options.now: Nobody catches you. That is the worst part.
later: Quest III opens with an empty case and Jai asking who he would report.

Own up and he forgives you (if you also kept his book, he wants that back first). Deny it and Marek's pattern book stays in its drawer: the stones are dressed rough, and the fair loaf can never be great.

options.now: A glass jar in two blankets and a cardigan.
later: The vigil cannot save her on its own. Only Tam's cutting can.

decisions.title: Who tells her
decisions.where: Quest II · the jar marked MUM
decisions.ask: Tam will give you a cup of the cutting he has kept alive for six years. He lets you choose the price.

options.now: At two in the morning, Noor sits down.
later: The Saturday loaf goes on the books.
At the fair you can offer the oven in Noor's name.
The Long Table becomes possible.

options.now: You can fold it in at four while she sleeps.
later: If you share the oven at the fair, Tam almost says it in front of her.
Vera can taste where the Mother has been, and asks whose kitchen, out loud.
When it comes out, it costs you with Noor.

options.pick: Leave the jar where it is
options.now: Her way: rye and the night.
later: If the vigil holds, the line is unbroken, and Vera asks no questions at the fair.
If it fails, the Mother is lost, and the jar becomes the only way home in Quest V.

decisions.title: The four o'clock feed
decisions.ask: Noor is asleep. The tap takes a while to run warm. The kettle has just boiled.

options.now: A little before five, a bubble.
later: The Mother lives, if she had the crock or the cutting.

options.now: “Asking is cheaper than guessing.”
later: Same as feeding her right, as long as the crock is there.

options.now: The smell changes. Oda warned you in so many words.
later: With the jar in your pocket you can start her again from Tam's six years, and must tell Noor everything.
Without it, the Mother is gone, Noor knows whose hand it was, and the career goes on without her.

decisions.title: Whose mark
decisions.ask: You have recut the stone. A dresser signs the work. Marek's ear of wheat is already there.

options.now: “That's the right kind of pride.”
later: Oda's regard.

options.now: “He'd have liked the cheek.”
later: Your mark is on the last millstone in the valley for as long as it turns.

options.now: A millrind, cut by a steady hand. “Now she's both of ours.”
later: The highest standing with Oda in the career.

decisions.title: The kitchen table
decisions.ask: Suvi signs the whole harvest away at the end of the week. She is not wrong to. The Red goes with it unless somebody makes it worth four awkward acres.

options.pick: Noor's price and a second buyer
options.now: Suvi strikes the Red out of the contract. Len puts the kettle on, which for Len is a speech.
later: Needs Mei's regard, or your own market stall from A stall of your own.
With dressed stones, the fair loaf is the best bread the Oven can make, so long as the Mother lives and the plait stays at home.

options.now: “Half's a seed crop. You can come back from half.”
later: Enough Red for the fair loaf and for Saturdays.

options.now: The farm is safe. Len walks the Red that night.
later: The fair loaf has ordinary flour in it and can never be great.
Suvi offers you an introducer's fee. Take it, and it is yours to confess to Noor or keep quiet about.

decisions.title: Forty minutes
decisions.ask: Tam's van is dead and his loaf is collapsing. The only hot oven in walking distance is his sister's.

options.now: He carries the tray up Baker Street himself and stops at the step.
later: Great loaf: the token comes home as “the bread with two bakers behind it”.
Lesser loaf: Tam wins in your fire, cannot bear it, and brings the token to your alley, unless the Mother was lost.
Either way, this is the door he walks through in Quest V.

options.pick: Hire it out for twenty brix
options.now: “The most Eastgate thing anyone on Baker Street has ever said.”
later: Vera mentions the landlord at the judging table.
Closes the Long Table. If his loaf wins, he still brings the token to your alley, unless the Mother was lost.

options.now: “Her words, near enough. Six years ago.”
later: You may still win, to a quiet square.
In Quest V Tam comes to the alley with a job offer, unless the Mother was lost, when he comes about that.

decisions.title: What the Oven should be
decisions.ask: Noor cannot shape a batch any more. She asks you what the bakery becomes. Only the answers you have earned are on the table.

options.now: Noor opens the side door herself.
later: Needs: you shared the oven at the fair, Tam is waiting in the alley, and either Noor knows about the cutting or the jar comes home that night.
The Town Oven burns again on market days.

options.now: Tam carries the jar in with both hands.
later: Only when the Mother was lost, and you get Tam to bring the jar home.

options.now: “Same size. Smaller would be false and larger would be cheek.”
later: Needs high standing with Noor.

options.now: Open unless the jar is coming home. The Oven goes on.
later: “It's lonelier than it looks, the name part.”

options.now: A third jar of the Mother, and a stall.
later: Needs A stall of your own, and a living Mother.

options.now: “Somebody in that mall should know what a door is for.”
later: Only if you shut the door at the fair and the Mother still lives. The best wage in the career.

decisions.title: Twenty minutes with Mei
decisions.ask: Everybody tells Mei things. She has a hundred things to tell you, and twenty minutes.

options.pick: Ask her where she would go
options.now: “Nobody asks me that.” She has never ridden the tram past Market Square.
later: Regard +20, which reaches 45 even from the lowest start.
Promise her the end of the line, and that promise is the next quest.

options.now: A good twenty minutes. She learns nothing about what you think of her.
later: Regard +10: courting begins. Whether that reaches 45 for dinner depends on where you started.

options.now: “It was a lovely loaf, truly.”
later: Nothing begins. You can ask again next week.

decisions.title: Her conditions
decisions.ask: Mei wants a home that is yours and 150 Bx put by before she will say yes. She has lived her whole life behind thin walls, and wants a door nobody else has a key to.

options.pick: Go and get them, then ask again
options.now: Two goals appear: own a home, and have 150 Bx across cash and accounts.
later: A mortgage counts; a rented room does not.
You ask again at the new door, and she says yes.

options.now: She skips her own speech. “Who does it in that order?” “A baker. We prove things first.”
later: Yes on the spot.

options.now: “I'd rather wait than marry a maybe.”
later: Regard −10. You are still walking out, and can ask again.

decisions.title: What do we do first?
decisions.where: The wedding · two coats in the hall
decisions.ask: The last choice of the quest line. It picks which end-game thread opens first; the others stay open.

options.now: “Two. And thick walls. And they'll both be told everything.”
later: End game opens on the family.

options.now: The empty shop between the café and the oven. “We could have it inside the year.”
later: End game opens on the fortune.

options.now: For once.
later: End game opens with nothing pressed.

careers_ahead.title: The Courier
careers_ahead.premise: Abe's knees are going and he has forty years of undeliverable post in a drawer at the depot: letters with no street, parcels for people who moved. You inherit the rounds and the drawer. Each dead letter is a small story with two ends, and one of them is addressed to a baker's son who left on a Tuesday.

careers_ahead.title: The Museum Hand
careers_ahead.premise: Eleven brass tokens have no family against their number, and Jai cannot sleep. You trace them through attics, wills and one very old grudge. Token number one is missing entirely. Vera knows who had it and has been waiting sixty years for somebody to ask politely.

careers_ahead.title: The Teller
careers_ahead.premise: When the wall came down, the town opened an account at Linden Bank “for the next thing we build together”, and never agreed what that was. A hundred and twenty years of interest later, you are the junior teller who finds it. Everyone in town has an opinion. Several of them have loan applications.

careers_ahead.title: The Gardener
careers_ahead.premise: Every street that ended at the wall was given a tree. The linden is dying, and the council will replace it with a bench. Hari means to save it at night, with his own money, and needs somebody who can keep a secret better than the last time.

careers_ahead.title: The Clinic Nurse
careers_ahead.premise: People tell a nurse what they tell nobody else. Noor's hands, Len's knee, Pip's sleeping, Vera's fear that her tasting memory is going. A career about what you do with what you are told, and when keeping a confidence stops being kind.

careers_ahead.title: The Estate Agent
careers_ahead.premise: The town's two property companies both want the row on Baker Street. Vera's flat is in it. So is a bakery. You hold the keys to half the town and learn that every one of them is somebody's four o'clock door.

additions.what: Flags that carry between quest lines
additions.why: Today flags are kept per resident. About thirty flags carry from one quest to a later one; the rest are read inside the quest that sets them.

additions.what: Reading another quest's ending in a reply or a start
additions.why: “done:new_in_town:gift” and the like. Today only a quest's own “needs” list and jobs read endings.

additions.what: A stage that opens on different lines depending on what happened
additions.why: Mei greets you differently if the count is short. One start node per condition, first match wins.
A few moments have no speaker: counting the barrow, the four o'clock feed. They are shown as text, not voiced. Stage directions on a spoken line are also text only, for the animators.

additions.what: Seven residents, four places, about a dozen items
additions.why: Noor, Tam, Pip, Oda, Suvi, Len, Vera; the Stone Oven, Crumb & Co's counter in Eastgate Mall, the mill house at Mill Fields, Brook Farm's kitchen; keys, the crock, rye, the jar, the token.
Mei's regard of 10 or more makes her a buyer for the Red; Noor's of 40 or more opens the partnership.

additions.what: Reputation gates on whole quest lines
additions.why: The courting quests each need her regard at a level before they are offered (25, 45 and 75). “Regard” on this page is the slice's reputation, −100 to 100.

additions.what: A goal for owning a home
additions.why: The proposal needs a home you own. The property market already knows what you own; the quest format needs a goal and a condition that read it. The money goal exists already.

additions.what: Courting, marriage and the end game as features
additions.why: None of these is in the backlog yet. Romance, a spouse who moves into your home, children and the wealth thread each need a backlog entry and a level picked before anything is built.

Every regard level, the 150 Bx and all rewards are placeholders until balanced against what a player earns. Some amounts are also spoken in lines (“a hundred and fifty brix”, “twenty brix”), and those lines have to change with the numbers.

Four endings can be taken again (turned away at the bakery, a lunch or dinner that goes badly, a proposal withdrawn). Taken again, the quest starts clean: the flags and items its own replies gave are cleared and the regard they awarded is taken back, so failing on purpose earns nothing. What the ending itself cost stays.
A few facts stop being true: the Mother is no longer lost once the jar comes home; a secret is no longer kept once it is out. The format today can only set flags.

additions.what: Facts that cannot both be true
additions.why: Sixteen groups of flags are exclusive (how the Mother ended, what you did with the oven, which loaf you entered). The checker now fails if two in a group are ever set together.
A talk stage is with one resident today. Several scenes here have two or more people speaking in turn: the first morning, the farm kitchen, the fair, the last door, the wedding.

additions.what: Quest items that cannot be sold
additions.why: The crock, the rye, Marek's tools, the fair token and the keys are held for the story. They should be marked as quest items so they cannot go on a stall.

additions.what: People and places not counted above
additions.why: Bram, who owns the Tram Café; the café's cook; Mrs Ellery of the museum committee; the tram depot and the field behind it at the end of the line. Two outlets in Eastgate Mall are already named Crumb, so Tam's counter can be one of them.
Decided by the owner: no quest is tied to a time of year. The fair is the Town Fair, held when the career reaches it, and nothing in the wording names a season or a month.

Decided by the owner: every player has their own copy of the career and the courting. Marrying Mei, losing the Mother or winning the fair happens in that player's game only, and other players in the same city do not see it. So all of this (flags, quest progress, regard, who is married, the lines residents say) is kept per player, and a resident such as Mei must be able to differ from one player's view to another's.

Decided by the owner. The world data has resident r0505, Jai, as a barista at the Tram Café; the live starter quest and this career both put him at the Old Town Museum. When this is built, his job and workplace in the world data change to the museum (keeper, on the museum's staff). He still shares the flat at Lantern Court with Mei.

Decided by the owner. The live starter quest greets the player with “Welcome to Linden!”; that one line changes to “Welcome to Old Town!” when this is built. Linden stays the name of the street and the bank. The copy of the live quests on this page still shows the line as it is in the game today.
Each of the four lines that can be taken again opens on a different line the second time (“You again.”), so the format needs to know that a line has been tried.

Three replies move money outside an ending: the mall loaf (4 Bx paid), the introducer's fee (30 Bx received) and the oven hire (20 Bx received). Each needs a ledger entry with a named other side: the mall's till, Valley Provisions, Tam's outlet.

additions.what: Regard with someone who is not in the conversation
additions.why: Several replies change regard with a person who is not the one speaking (Pip, when you answer Noor; Hari and Vera at the judging table). Three replies are gated on Tam's or Pip's regard.

The Town Oven on the square, lit on market days after the Long Table ending, and the empty chandler's shop next to the café. The breakfast loaf should be eaten or unsellable. Ninety-one residents are already named Noor; the baker is the one at the Stone Oven.

additions.what: What the world shows is per player too
additions.why: Following the owner's decision that the story is each player's own: the lit Town Oven, the line added to the bakery's sign and who lives where after the wedding are seen only by the player whose story it is.

additions.what: Two checks in the live validator
additions.why: The game's quest checker rejects a line whose replies all carry a condition, and a negated money need. About thirty lines here have a condition on every reply: most are pairs of opposites (if / unless), and a few are covered by facts that cannot both be true, and the proposal uses “has not 150 Bx” and “has no home”. The checker needs to accept a set of conditions that covers every case.

The rare book from Errand runner can be sold today. If it is sold, the only way to mend things with Jai is gone, and one of his lines (“I still have the book”) can be false. It should not be sellable while that thread is open.
Dough Hand to Master Baker, wages and a share of takings rest on the career requirements (CAR-001 to CAR-005), which are still only proposed in the spec.
